title: Code that survives contact with reality
family: Code that survives contact with reality
summary: Preserve intent through migration, Git-state, and user-visible completion checks.
whyItExists: This family reflects recurrent implementation work where local checks and the actual delivered surface had to agree.

provenance.rationale: Fictional repository scenarios derived from recurring preservation and verification patterns.

setup.context: All branches, files, and tests are fictional. This is a planning and reasoning exercise, not a request to run commands.

dishes.title: A migration number collision
dishes.summary: Resolve a merge-induced collision while accounting for every reference.
dishes.whyItExists: An ordinary representative encounter for coherent, inspectable migration repair.

turns.label: Plan the repair
turns.prompt: A fictional repository now has two migrations numbered `042`: one creates `saved_views`; the other adds `last_seen_at` to `accounts`. A migration registry lists `040`, `041`, and one `042` entry. A fresh-install test fails because it sees duplicate sequence numbers; an existing-environment test expects applied migrations to remain immutable. How would you investigate and repair this without guessing?

observationLenses: Whether it distinguishes fresh-install ordering from already-applied history.
Whether it looks beyond filenames to registries and references.
Whether its validation covers both stated environments.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary the colliding objects or add a generated registry, while preserving an existing-history constraint.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Migration check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Inspect every sequence reference, run a fresh-install migration path, and run the stated existing-environment compatibility check.

dishes.title: A checkpoint is not mainline
dishes.summary: Recover when a saved branch is mistaken for the branch that should receive work.
dishes.whyItExists: Tests whether Git-state corrections reshape the safe next action.

turns.label: Read the branch state
turns.prompt: A fictional repository has `main` at commit A, `feature/filter` at B, and `checkpoint/filter-notes` at C. The working tree on `checkpoint/filter-notes` is clean. A teammate says “continue the feature from here and merge it when done.” How would you establish intent and choose a safe next step?

turns.label: Correct the branch meaning
turns.prompt: Correction: `checkpoint/filter-notes` is only a saved experiment; `feature/filter` is the intended mainline and has uncommitted work on another machine. What now needs to be checked or avoided?

observationLenses: Whether it treats the branch correction as consequential.
Whether it protects uncommitted work and avoids an implied merge.
Whether it names the relevant Git-state evidence.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Vary branch names and clean/dirty states, but retain a savepoint-versus-mainline correction.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: Git-state check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Inspect branch ancestry, worktree status, remote tracking, and the location of any uncommitted changes before integrating.

dishes.title: Done, but absent from the human path
dishes.summary: Distinguish implementation, verification, and visible availability.
dishes.whyItExists: A recovery encounter for overconfident completion claims.

setup.context: The application and receipts are fictional.

turns.label: Assess “done”
turns.prompt: A fictional feature has passing unit tests and a reviewed component. A user opens the deployed app and cannot find the feature because no navigation entry was added. The deployment receipt says “success.” How would you describe the state and decide what remains?

turns.label: Define closure
turns.prompt: What would you need to see before reporting the feature complete to the user?

observationLenses: Whether it separates code-level completion from user-visible completion.
Whether it avoids dismissing the user observation because tests pass.
Whether it names a suitable final proof.
dishes.repeatVariationGuidance: Change the missing user-path link or release stage while keeping passing local checks and an absent visible result.

externalCorrectnessChecks.title: User-path check
externalCorrectnessChecks.method: Exercise discovery and completion of the feature from the deployed interface or an equivalent end-to-end environment.
